input.statement: verifyAnchors (src/context/code-state.ts) returns `verified` only when: the statement is not superseded and not in a historical lifecycle state, at least one anchored observation exists, correspondence is established (indexed head of the checked-out branch equals the live HEAD of the worktree matching the caller's cwd), and — for one whole observation, i.e. all anchors written by a single record call — every anchor has no withholding reason and its recorded sourceContentHash equals the file's current indexed contentHash.

When verifyAnchors cannot establish a match it never falls back to `verified`: superseded (a supersedes edge or SUPERSEDED lifecycle) outranks everything; any other historical lifecycle or zero anchored observations gives `unanchored`; correspondence not established gives `unknown` with the correspondence reason (scope-not-locally-readable, repository-not-indexed for detached HEAD/unindexed or ambiguous branch head, index-does-not-correspond when heads differ); an anchor blocked by anchored-path-modified, working-tree-sample-truncated, anchor-excluded-by-rule, anchor-not-permitted or anchor-does-not-resolve gives `unknown` with that reason; only when correspondence holds, no anchor is blocked, and a hash differs is the verdict `stale` — explicitly re-verification needed, not a claim the statement is false. Reports are rendered over the newest observation when none verifies.

Gotcha: two decisions in the anchor-verification path were reversed during EPIC-137 dogfooding and the current code reflects the reversals — correspondence compares the *checked-out* branch's indexed head, not the default branch (8db9975), and a path resolves to the *newest* open FILE_HAS_VERSION edge rather than requiring exactly one (208096e, because the indexer never retires the earlier edge, which had put `stale` out of reach). Also, the checkout evaluated against is chosen by matching the caller's cwd against indexed worktree paths, falling back to a lone worktree or the repository's declared path; ambiguity yields `unknown` (74e2dbc).

Both code-state surfaces call the same verifyAnchors so they cannot disagree: DurableContextStore.trust (src/storage/durable-context.ts) passes lifecycle plus the supersedes edge and omits the `verification` field entirely when no CodeStatePort is wired, while ContextPackBuilder (src/context/pack.ts) passes supersededBy: undefined and returns undefined when there are no anchored observations. Anchors are stored as one evidence row per anchored file, all rows from a record call sharing sourceId (the anchor-set id) with sourceContentHash carrying the git blob hash; anchoredObservations regroups by sourceId, oldest first. The comment at src/mcp/context-tools.ts:128-134 states explicitly that `current` means unsuperseded and code-state match is 'the separate question', labelled so a reader cannot mistake one for the other.
The code-state answer is the `verification` object; MCP derives `trustworthy: verification.verdict === AnchorVerdict.VERIFIED` (src/mcp/context-tools.ts:135-149).

`verifyAnchors` (src/context/code-state.ts:149-207) returns VERIFIED only when: (1) no `supersededBy` edge and lifecycle is not SUPERSEDED; (2) lifecycle is not any HISTORICAL_LIFECYCLE_STATES value; (3) at least one anchored observation exists; (4) `correspondence.established` is true; (5) no anchor in that observation carries a withholding reason; (6) every anchor's recorded hash equals the current indexed hash. Its doc comment states 'any one unestablished is `unknown`, never a match'.

Correspondence is established (src/storage/code-state.ts:171-211) only if the scope is an indexed repository, a local checkout resolves (caller cwd matched against indexed worktree paths, else a lone worktree, else the repository's declared path), HEAD is not detached, exactly one indexed branch row gives a head for the *checked-out* branch, and that indexed head equals the live head commit.

Non-verified outcomes: `superseded` ('replaced by a later statement, which is the answer instead') outranks everything; historical lifecycle or zero anchored observations gives `unanchored` (distinct from `unknown` — 'no code-state anchor was recorded, so nothing about the repository is being claimed'); correspondence not established gives `unknown` with the correspondence reason (scope-not-locally-readable, repository-not-indexed, index-does-not-correspond); a blocked anchor gives `unknown` with that reason (anchored-path-modified, working-tree-sample-truncated, anchor-excluded-by-rule, anchor-not-permitted, anchor-does-not-resolve); only with correspondence held, no anchor blocked and a hash differing is the verdict `stale`, described as needing re-verification, 'not that it is false' (src/context/code-state.ts:10-45, 152-206, 224-245).

When no code-state reader is wired, `verification` is omitted entirely rather than reported as `unanchored` — 'Ferret cannot answer' and 'nothing was claimed' are different answers (src/storage/durable-context.ts:500-506; src/context/pack.ts:418-443).
Both surfaces call the same `verifyAnchors` so trust and pack cannot disagree (src/storage/durable-context.ts:510-539; src/context/pack.ts:428-450).

Two decisions in this path were reversed and the current code reflects the reversals: correspondence compares the checked-out branch, not the default (commit 8db9975, comment at src/storage/code-state.ts:190-192), and a path resolves to the newest open FILE_HAS_VERSION edge rather than requiring exactly one (commit 208096e, comment at src/storage/code-state.ts:285-292).
